prompts.text: Is there something inexpensive you collect because every piece has a story?
Tell me about an ordinary object you've kept longer than anybody would expect.
You spot a tiny antique shop while we're passing. What would draw you inside?
A collection of postcards from places you've visited or tickets from events you've enjoyed?
The things people choose to keep sometimes explain their memories better than photographs do.
A souvenir doesn't have to be pretty if it reminds you of a good day.
What's the strangest item you've seen proudly displayed in someone's home?
I find a battered old coin while clearing a drawer. What would you want to know about it?
Picking a small memento for one another at a market or finding something useful we can both make?
Tell me the story behind something you own that would look unremarkable to a stranger.
What's a subject you could give a five-minute talk about without preparing?
People become noticeably more animated when someone asks about a very specific interest.
You're explaining something you're passionate about and I keep asking basic questions. What makes that enjoyable rather than tiring?
Learning how a camera works or finding out how your favourite dessert is made?
When did you last discover that somebody you knew had a completely unexpected skill?
Being genuinely interested in somebody's hobby beats pretending you already understand it.
Have you learned a skill from watching somebody work rather than taking lessons?
We're at a workshop and the instructor asks one of us to demonstrate first. Who volunteers?
A short introduction to woodworking or a beginner session on film photography?
Tell me about a subject you dismissed at school but became curious about years later.
When people visit you, what's the first thing you usually offer them?
I show up for a casual visit and you've accidentally invited three other people. How do we make it less awkward?
A good host notices when guests need space as well as when they need attention.
An outdoor get-together with shared food or a small dinner where everyone helps cook?
Tell me about a home you visited that immediately felt welcoming.
Every family has its own unspoken rules about taking the last piece of food.
Do you prefer bringing a little something when you visit somebody or helping with the preparations?
We're the first guests to arrive and the host is still cooking. What would you offer to do?
Helping to set the table or taking responsibility for the music?
What's the funniest household custom you've had to explain to a visitor?
A person who notices the architecture on an ordinary street can make a short walk interesting.
What detail do you tend to notice first when you enter somewhere unfamiliar?
We pass a building with an unusual door and no sign. What's your theory about what happens inside?
People-watching from a quiet bench or exploring little side streets with interesting shopfronts?
Tell me about a detail you spotted that everybody else walked past.
Being observant doesn't necessarily mean being quiet; sometimes it makes you ask better questions.
Have you ever recognised a place in real life because you saw it in a photograph years earlier?
I challenge you to find five unusual things during a ten-minute walk. What counts as unusual?
An afternoon spotting street art or trying to recognise different birds by their calls?
What's an ordinary sound that takes you straight back to a specific memory?
Tell me about a day you got lost but still ended up somewhere worth discovering.
Are you more likely to ask for directions immediately or try to work things out first?
We're following a map that keeps sending us in circles. Who admits defeat first?
Being able to laugh when plans go wrong makes an outing much easier.
Accidentally ending up at a local fair or finding a tiny café on the wrong street?
The funniest travel stories sometimes begin with somebody misreading one small sign.
Have you ever taken the wrong bus or train and met someone interesting along the way?
The venue we planned to visit has moved without updating its address. What's our backup?
A carefully researched route with stops or a leisurely wander where we ask locals for ideas?
Tell me about a small mistake you made that eventually became a family story.
What's your definition of a day off that actually feels restful?
Having nowhere urgent to be can make a short conversation feel luxurious.
Our plan gets cancelled and we unexpectedly have the afternoon free. What would you enjoy doing instead?
Sitting outside watching the world go by or spending an afternoon inside with a good book?
Tell me about the last time you enjoyed doing almost nothing without feeling guilty.
People who say they want to relax often have surprisingly elaborate ideas of what relaxing involves.
Are you comfortable leaving a weekend completely unplanned?
I suggest putting our phones away for twenty minutes at a café. Would that feel relaxing or odd?
Listening to the rain from indoors or finding a shady place to sit on a bright day?
You don't have to fill every silence to make somebody feel welcome.
What's a part of your work or studies that outsiders usually misunderstand?
Tell me about a surprisingly interesting person you met through something you were working on.
You have to explain your job to a curious ten-year-old in two sentences. How would you do it?
A job with lots of different people to meet or one where you can focus quietly for long stretches?
People's least glamorous work stories are sometimes the most entertaining.
Being proud of a small piece of work is worth celebrating even if nobody else sees it.
If you could shadow someone in any profession for a day, whose day would you choose?
We're chatting with someone who has a job neither of us understands. What's your first question?
Learning a useful trade for one week or spending a week behind the scenes of a theatre?
What practical lesson from your first job has stayed with you?
What's something you used to dislike but would happily choose now?
Tell me about the first time your opinion changed because you gave something a second chance.
It's more interesting when someone can explain how their taste changed than defend a favourite forever.
I bring a snack you haven't tried since childhood. Do you risk seeing whether you still hate it?
Revisiting a song you once couldn't stand or trying a dish you refused to eat as a child?
The foods we reject as children sometimes become the ones we order most often.
Has a friend ever changed your mind about a place you thought you'd never enjoy?
You loved a film years ago, but the rewatch disappoints you. Do you admit it or protect the memory?
Trying a completely unfamiliar cuisine or giving an old least-favourite dish another chance?
What's one preference you expect future-you might laugh about?
What's a little thing you were nervous to try that turned out to be easier than expected?
Doing something unfamiliar without making a spectacle of it can still be a brave decision.
You want to go to a community event but don't know anybody there. What would help you walk in?
Asking a stranger for a recommendation or volunteering to speak briefly to a small group?
Tell me about a time you surprised yourself by saying yes to something new.
People often describe their everyday courage as though it was no big deal.
Is there an ordinary activity you avoided for years before finally trying it?
I'm learning to skate and falling over constantly. Would you join in or cheer from the side?
A beginner's public speaking workshop or a friendly improv game with no audience?
Who has helped you feel confident enough to be a beginner at something?
What's a place that makes conversation feel easier, even when you don't know someone very well?
We're at a busy gathering and find the one quiet corner. What would you want to talk about there?
Talking while travelling somewhere or sitting down properly once we arrive?
Different spaces seem to bring out different sides of the same person.
Choosing a comfortable place matters more than planning the perfect conversation topics.
Tell me about a memorable chat that happened somewhere completely unexpected.
Do you notice the atmosphere of a place before you notice who's there?
We arrive at a beautiful outdoor spot only to discover there are no seats. How do we adapt?
A little balcony overlooking the street or a shaded courtyard away from the noise?
What's a place you once visited that immediately made you want to return with somebody?
